subject: Horizon Payments — Access orchestration & SSO/SCIM handoff
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonpay.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Laura Jenkins <l.jenkins@horizonpay.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Ready to kick off SSO/SCIM + IP allowlist

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intros. We’re aiming to start SSO/SCIM cutover for Horizon Payments next week and want to confirm the sequence and responsibilities so procurement and security can align. High level asks from our side:
- SSO (SAML): metadata endpoint + EntityID you expect from us
- SCIM: server-to-server token and provisioning scope
- IP allowlist: formats you accept (CIDR vs single IP) and test ranges
- Service accounts: what permissions Redwood needs for the SCIM service account
- Audit / retention: where logs live and retention windows

Can you share a simple mutual action plan (MAP) and checklist we can attach to the internal ticket? We’d like to target a staged cutover: test tenant on Dec 28, go-live Dec 30 (flexible).

I can loop in security@horizonpay.com to share the org policy constraints.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager
Horizon Payments

Hi Samir — great, thanks. Attaching our "redwood-sso-scim-checklist.docx" (stub) and an IP template. Quick notes and proposed next steps: 

1) Deliverables we need from Horizon
   - SAML metadata XML (entityID, sign cert, ACS URL)
   - SCIM service account token + required attributes for provisioning (email, displayName, groups)
   - Test user account (email) for validation
   - IP ranges for both test and production environments (CSV or CIDR ok)

2) Redwood deliverables
   - MAP doc + checklist (attached)
   - Temporary test routing for prefix caching and SCIM staging
   - Audit log endpoints and retention policy summary

3) Roles / owners
   - Horizon: Laura Jenkins (procurement) for contract/whitelisting windows; Security contact for org policy
   - Redwood: myself (CS lead) for MAP; Neha (engineer) for SAML/SCIM config; Ben (infra) for IP allowlist and network test

4) Proposed timeline
   - Wed 12/21: 30m technical alignment (SAML payload + SCIM token)
   - Tue 12/28: test tenant cutover (non-prod)
   - Thu 12/30: go-live (production) — flexible by 24h

Can we do a quick alignment call Wed 12/21 10:00 AM ET? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a link to the MAP in Drive.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): redwood-sso-scim-checklist.docx (checklist stub), ip-allowlist-template.csv (CSV template)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 11:10:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Ready to kick off SSO/SCIM + IP allowlist

Hi all — adding a few technical clarifications before the Wed call so Horizon can prep: 

- SAML: We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. For the initial cutover we prefer SP-initiated. Please provide a metadata XML and the signing cert in DER or PEM. ACS URL will be provided in the MAP.
- SCIM: We expect a Bearer token for auth. Token should have a scope limited to user:write, user:read, group:read. We do not store full tokens in plaintext; we request a scoped service account with the minimum privileges required for provisioning.
- Service account: name convention preferred: horizon-scim-redwood. The account needs: read/write on users, read on groups; nothing beyond that.
- IP allowlist: we accept CIDR ranges; please include both egress and ingress ranges if your network policy varies. Template attached.
- Org policies: If Horizon enforces device posture or SSO restrictions by OU/policy, please include the documentation or a policy owner we can test against.

I’ll prepare a short runbook snippet to include in the MAP (validation steps for user create/update, group sync, rollback).

-Neha
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2027 09:30:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Ready to kick off SSO/SCIM + IP allowlist

Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the metadata. For the allowlist, we tested with the CSV format in the template; the values we usually need from customers are: public egress IPs for your NAT, and any inbound CIDR blocks we should accept for management endpoints. For Horizon I suggest providing two rows: test and prod ranges. Example: 203.0.113.0/24 (test), 198.51.100.0/24 (prod).

On Dedicated vs Hosted: if you’ll be on Redwood Dedicated, we can add the ranges at the infra layer — otherwise for Hosted API we’ll apply allowlist at the tenancy level. Either way the template is fine.

I’ve also added a short validation checklist to the MAP: create test user, force sync, verify group membership, verify login via IdP, check audit entries.

-ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): ip-allowlist-template.csv
